I farm 1.26 hectares of beans here in the North East, but the land is rented so I must watch my spending carefully. Beans fix their own nitrogen, so I will not buy expensive chemical fertilizer this season; instead I will spread manure to keep the soil fertile. I plant local bean seeds because improved ones are costly and hard to find in our market, but I will buy pesticide because bean pests can ruin the whole harvest if left alone. My family will do most of the work—weeding and picking beans takes many hands—and I will hire about thirty days of labor when the weeding and harvest come at once.
